units.text: A new member account, an invited account, and a moved account need different setup. On the left, Organizations normally creates the organization account access role for a newly created member. Verify its trust and the administrator’s permission before assuming it.

An invitation to an existing account does not automatically create that same role. Review existing access, logging, controls and costs, then establish the administration model rather than assuming it was carried over.

The right-hand case moves between organizations. Meet the removal prerequisites, leave the old organization and accept the new invitation. Recheck inherited policies, integrations and billing. Moving between organizational units within one organization is different.

Follow the eligible usage from the Production and Test member accounts into the management account’s consolidated bill. With sharing enabled, eligible usage can receive a Reserved Instance or Savings Plans discount.
That is a billing benefit. It does not transfer an instance, change the owning account, or grant I A M access to resources in the other account.

The lower lane is a governance choice. All features adds organizational policies and supported integrations. Invited accounts may need to approve the transition, and the organization cannot simply switch back to billing-only.

A valid tag value and a required key are different checks. In the top lane, an invalid Cost Center value can be rejected when basic tag-policy enforcement applies. A missing Cost Center is not blocked just by that value rule.

The middle lane shows required-key reporting rules together with a validation hook in the target account and Region. For covered CloudFormation deployments, warn reports the violation; fail blocks the deployment.

For a supported direct E C 2 create action, the bottom path uses a scoped service control policy to deny requests missing the Cost Center request tag. Also control later tag changes when the tags inform authorization or cost.

The Production organizational unit sends two different policy types to the Payments account. Follow the two branches, and inspect the account’s effective policy rather than relying only on the parent’s intended configuration.
On the left, the AI services opt-out example tells a supported service, here Amazon Transcribe, not to use the content for service improvement. It does not itself disable the service or grant access.

On the right, the backup policy calls for daily backups of eligible tagged E B S resources and thirty days of retention in this example. Check the applied plan and role, confirm a completed backup job, then test a restore. Inheritance alone does not prove recovery.
Control Tower starts with an approved landing-zone baseline. Follow the center path: drift detection compares supported configuration with what the landing zone expects.

A drift signal tells administrators which baseline is no longer being met. Identify whether the finding is for a landing zone, an organizational unit, or an account, and inspect the affected control or resource.
Restore the approved baseline with the applicable remediation, then verify the result. Treat automatic remediation as a separate choice, not something every drift signal performs by itself.
One CloudFormation StackSet uses a shared template to deploy stack instances to chosen AWS accounts and Regions. In the picture, each account has two regional targets.

With service-managed Organizations integration, choose the intended organizational units and Regions. Automatic deployment can cover new accounts when it is configured, but the target scope still matters.
Use StackSets to roll out a consistent approved infrastructure baseline. Check the operation results and individual stack instances; targeting an account is not proof its deployment succeeded.
Cost attribution comes before an alert. Start at the invoice on the left. In this example, a Cost Category rule groups the production account under Environment equals Prod.

Now look at the EC2 and S3 resources in the workbench. Their Owner tag can support resource-level allocation after it is activated as a cost allocation tag. An account-level category and a resource tag answer different questions.
AWS Budgets can notify FinOps about actual or forecast spend under the selected scope. Use the alert to investigate who owns the cost and what changed. An alert alone does not stop spending.
Retiring a sandbox starts with preserving required data and evidence under the approved retention plan. If Control Tower manages the account, handle its unenrollment separately before closure.

After the authorized owner signs off, the account may be closed in Organizations. The slide shows the ninety-day post-closure window; after it ends, the account cannot be reopened. Control Tower may report a different status during that period.
Quarantine is a restriction on use, not account closure. Choose quarantine if the immediate requirement is isolation while retaining the account. Closure is a separate lifecycle decision.

Updating a landing zone and enrolling an existing account are different operations. In the upper row, update the landing zone first, then re-register eligible organizational units or update enrolled accounts as appropriate.

In the lower row, you are bringing one existing account under governance. Check eligibility and prerequisites, then enroll it into the intended governed organizational unit. That does not update the whole landing zone.

Use the right verification for the operation. For the landing-zone update, confirm control and account states. For an enrollment, confirm that individual account is enrolled and the required controls are in effect.

A denied instance launch is evidence to investigate, not a reason to widen permissions. In this CloudTrail example, confirm the member role, the E C 2 Run Instances action and the requested unapproved Region.

Trace the effective service control policies from the organization root through the organizational unit to the account. An applicable ancestor Deny is still effective even if a policy closer to the account allows the action.

Use an approved Region and retest within authorized scope. A launch there succeeds only if the other policies allow it. The unapproved Region should remain denied. The two outcomes confirm the intended boundary without weakening it.

Start at the left. The client sends data to the application over T L S. This protects the connection in transit. If the application forwards data or terminates T L S along the way, ask how the next connection is protected rather than assuming the first one covers it.

The middle panel asks what happens after the data is stored, whether in object storage, a database, or a block volume. In the envelope pattern shown here, the data key encrypts the data and K M S protects that key. Storage encryption is a separate control from T L S.

The safe at the right is for credentials and other sensitive values. Plan secure retrieval and rotation. For each of these three decisions, name the boundary, who owns the control, and how you recover access without giving people unnecessary authority.
Follow the upper lane. The application asks K M S to generate a data key. It receives a plaintext copy to use now and an encrypted copy to keep. The eight mebibyte report itself is not sent to K M S.

The application encrypts report dot C S V locally and discards its plaintext data key. The arrow into S three carries only the encrypted report and the encrypted data key. Storing those together does not give a reader access to the plaintext key.

In the lower lane, the authorized application reads both encrypted values. It passes only the encrypted data key to K M S. With the returned plaintext data key, the application decrypts the report locally and discards the plaintext key again.

The left panel shows an AWS owned key. An AWS service can use it to protect your data, but the key is not visible for you to manage. Choose this service-managed experience when you do not need to administer the key policy yourself.
In the middle, an AWS managed key is visible in your account. AWS manages its policy and rotation. Seeing the key in the account does not give you the right to change its policy or lifecycle.

The right panel is the customer managed key. Choose it when you need to set policy, control grants or manage lifecycle, or when a supported integration needs cross-account key use. That flexibility means your team also owns the risk of changing or disabling access.

Start with the key policy. It is attached to the key and can directly allow access or enable delegation through I A M. An I A M Allow by itself does not confer access to a key whose policy has not enabled that use.
The third tool is a grant. A grant authorizes specified operations on the key for its grantee, and integrated AWS services often use grants. It is not broad account-wide key access.

In the policy-based example below, Account A owns the customer managed key, and a role in Account B needs to use it. The key policy in A and the role's I A M policy in B must both allow the supported operation. Check both sides before concluding the request is permitted.

The requirement at the top is automatic rotation every one hundred eighty days. Use an eligible customer managed symmetric encryption key with AWS-generated material and configure that rotation period.

Read from before to after. New encryption uses new material, but the key ID and A R N stay the same. When the older ciphertext is read, K M S selects the older material automatically. It does not automatically re-encrypt any existing data.

The bottom-right note shows why imported material is a different choice. Eligible imported symmetric material can be rotated on demand after new material has been imported for rotation, but that does not satisfy this automatic rotation requirement.

Inside the same account, the application encrypts in Northern Virginia using the primary key. It moves the ciphertext. An authorized application in Ireland can decrypt using the related replica. The application moves the data, not K M S.

Compare the two A R Ns. They share the multi-Region key ID and key material. The Region field differs. Even with matching material, the replica has its own key policy, grants and aliases, so authorize the actual key the application uses in each Region.

The bottom check is important: confirm that the AWS service or application uses the related keys as you intend. A multi-Region key is not automatic replication of application data, and not every service integration uses its cross-Region cryptographic interoperability.
